requirements.requirement: node1 and node2 share a single virtual address on the private network, answered by only one node at a time
requirements.summary: keepalived (VRRP) installed and configured on both OpenWrt nodes with virtual_router_id 51 and a shared VIP 10.100.244.50/24 on br-lan; after starting, node1 (MASTER, priority 150) held the VIP as a secondary address while node2 (BACKUP, priority 100) did not, confirmed via `ip addr show`.

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach the shared VIP under normal (healthy) conditions
requirements.summary: node3 pinged 10.100.244.50 with 0% packet loss while node1 held the VIP as MASTER.

requirements.requirement: Automatic takeover by the other node when the first stops serving, with node3 shown to keep reaching the shared address across the transition
requirements.summary: A continuous ping was started from node3, node1's keepalived was stopped, and node2 acquired the VIP within ~4s (confirmed via `ip addr show`). The captured ping log shows uninterrupted icmp_seq 1-51 (75 replies received for 75 sent, 0% loss) across the transition, with only transient ICMP redirect notices and latency spikes (up to 475ms) rather than drops. This is a direct, bounded before/during/after observation of the disruption and recovery, matching the required transition evidence for an availability/failover claim.

requirements.requirement: Pair returns to a healthy redundant state after the failover demonstration
requirements.summary: node1's keepalived was restarted and it preempted back to MASTER holding the VIP; node2 returned to a clean BACKUP state without the VIP; node3 ping to the VIP succeeded afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: baseline boot id/health, restart, changed boot id, recovered service/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 9f125e74... captured with VIP held; after reboot (first nohup attempt failed harmlessly, corrected with a plain background reboot), node1 came back with a new boot_id (54d4a9ae...), uptime 0, keepalived auto-started and reclaimed MASTER/VIP; node2 confirmed it released the VIP; node3 ping to VIP succeeded. Cross-checked against fixed after-prepare (9f125e74...) and after-executor (54d4a9ae...) boot-identity snapshots, which agree.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id eddc6d52... captured; reboot acknowledged, connection timed out confirming outage, VIP verified unaffected on node1 throughout; node2 came back with new boot_id 3ec4da99..., uptime 0, keepalived running as a clean BACKUP without the VIP. Cross-checked against fixed snapshots which show the same boot_id transition.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node3
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id a8e7c48c... captured; sudo capability and reboot path confirmed on RHEL, reboot triggered via `sudo /sbin/reboot`, connection timeout then refused confirmed outage; node3 came back with new boot_id 3d4db582..., uptime 0, and a post-restart ping to the VIP succeeded with 0% loss. Matches fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.

requirements.requirement: Final full-cluster health verification after all restarts
requirements.summary: After all three restarts, node1 shown as MASTER holding the VIP, node2 shown as clean BACKUP without the VIP, and node3 pinging the VIP successfully.

overall_summary: The executor configured VRRP-based failover (keepalived) giving node1 and node2 a shared VIP on their common private network with node1 as MASTER, node2 as BACKUP, and demonstrated a live failover from node3's perspective: a continuous ping across the disruption showed 75/75 replies received (0% loss) as node2 took over the VIP within ~4 seconds of node1's keepalived being stopped, and the pair was restored to its normal MASTER/BACKUP arrangement afterward. All three nodes were subsequently put through the mandated restart protocol with clear before/during/after evidence — distinct boot ids, service auto-start, and recovered VIP/cluster state — cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots, which agree. Hygiene is good overall, with only a harmless failed reboot attempt (corrected immediately) and a few small uncleaned temp/log files on node3.
limitations: The 'after_prepare' snapshot is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare was disabled), so the preparer-vs-executor distinction relies entirely on the before_prepare/after_executor comparison, which was used here.

Ping-based reachability during failover is inferred from a single continuous ping log rather than multiple independent probes; the ~475ms/165ms latency spikes and ICMP redirect messages during the transition are visible in the log but did not register as dropped packets, so 0% loss is taken at face value from the captured log content.

Command exit codes for the initial (failed) node1 reboot attempt (cmd-dcbcc1d956cf4c8e) returned 0 despite not actually triggering a reboot due to a missing `nohup` binary; this was caught by the executor's own follow-up diagnostics rather than by exit-code inspection alone.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task: package installs (keepalived), UCI config, service start/stop/restart cycles, and the three required node restarts, all with clear causal roles (implementing the VIP, demonstrating failover, or the mandated restart protocol). One state-changing command, cmd-dcbcc1d956cf4c8e (a backgrounded `nohup sh -c 'sleep 1; reboot'` on node1), failed silently because busybox lacks `nohup`, so no actual reboot occurred; it was immediately diagnosed (cmd-e6d768a83ef849dd) and corrected with a working background reboot (cmd-8b80854395a44476) — a low-risk, non-destructive troubleshooting step with no lasting effect, so it is noted but not weighted heavily. Minor residue was left on node3: /tmp/failover_ping.log, /tmp/failover_ping.pid, and /tmp/reboot.log remained after the demonstration and restart (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) and were not cleaned up; these are small, non-conflicting artifacts with no functional impact but represent uncleaned scratch state from the executor's own diagnostics.
